saints.name: Charbel Makhlouf
saints.legacy: A model of prayer and healing
saints.summary: Charbel Makhlouf was a Maronite priest and hermit from Lebanon known for his deep spirituality and miraculous healings. He lived a life of extreme asceticism, dedicating himself to prayer and solitude in a hermitage for over two decades. After his death, numerous miracles attributed to him have drawn many pilgrims to his tomb, solidifying his legacy as a powerful intercessor.

saints.name: Tarsilla and Emiliana
saints.legacy: Models of virginity and spiritual perseverance
saints.summary: Tarsilla and Emiliana were two sisters and aunts of Saint Gregory the Great who dedicated their lives to God through virginity. They lived together in a spiritual community, encouraging each other in virtue while mourning their sister Gordiana's return to worldly ways. Their lives exemplify the importance of perseverance in faith and the call to a deeper spiritual life.

saints.name: Delphinus
saints.summary: Saint Delphinus was a Bishop of Bordeaux known for his strong defense of orthodox Christian teachings during the early Church. He played a significant role in condemning heretical movements, particularly at the Council of Saragossa in 380. His influence extended to notable figures such as Saint Paulinus, whom he baptized and inspired towards a life of holiness.
